title: Maximum Twin Sum of a List

concept.title: Pair the first half with the reversed second half
body: A list with an **even** number `n` of nodes has **twins**: node `i` and node `n - 1 - i` (the first and the last, the second and the second last, ...). You want the largest sum `value(i) + value(n - 1 - i)`.

This is the palindrome pattern again, with a sum instead of a comparison. Find the middle, **reverse the second half**, and walk the first half and the reversed second half at the same time: the two nodes you see are always twins.

body.code:
slow = fast = head
while fast is not None and fast.next is not None:
    slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next.next
prev = None                                    # reverse from the middle on
while slow is not None:
    nxt = slow.next; slow.next = prev; prev = slow; slow = nxt
best = 0
left, right = head, prev
while right is not None:
    best = max(best, left.val + right.val)
    left = left.next; right = right.next

body: Because `n` is even, the middle node is the first node of the second half, so the halves have the same length and the walk stops exactly at the end.

statement: A singly linked list has an even number `n` of nodes. The twin of the node at index `i` (counting from 0) is the node at index `n - 1 - i`. Print the largest value of `value(i) + value(n - 1 - i)` over all twin pairs.
inputFormat: The second line has the values of the nodes, from the head to the tail.

examples.note: The twin sums are 5 + 1 = 6 and 4 + 2 = 6: the maximum is 6.

hints: Find the middle node with a slow and a fast reference.
Reverse the second half of the list.
Walk both halves together and keep the largest sum.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

# Every node is also remembered in this list. Python in the browser cannot free a very long chain of nodes at once,
# so free_nodes() (called at the end) cuts the links first and the nodes are then freed one by one.
all_nodes = []


class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next
        all_nodes.append(self)


def free_nodes():
    for node in all_nodes:
        node.next = None
        if hasattr(node, "random"):
            node.random = None
    all_nodes.clear()


# Builds a list from the values. If pos is 0 or more, the last node points back to the node at index pos (a cycle).
def build_list(values, pos=-1):
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = ListNode(v, head)
    if pos >= 0:
        tail = head
        while tail.next is not None:
            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        for _ in range(pos):
            target = target.next
        tail.next = target
    return head


# Prints the values of a list on one line ("empty" for an empty list).
def print_list(head):
    out = []
    while head is not None:
        out.append(head.val)
        head = head.next
    print(*(out if out else ["empty"]))


def twin_sum(head):
    slow = fast = head
    while fast is not None and fast.next is not None:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
    prev = None
    while slow is not None:
        nxt = slow.next
        slow.next = prev
        prev = slow
        slow = nxt
    best = None
    left, right = head, prev
    while right is not None:
        s = left.val + right.val
        if best is None or s > best:
            best = s
        left = left.next
        right = right.next
    return best

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

print(twin_sum(build_list(a)))
free_nodes()
